sections.h2: Fastest way to sell in Oshkosh
sections.html:
Paperwork first, then the choice between listing and cash, which depends on the house's condition. Three items are worth settling before you start: the permit record for your address, the condition report, and a deed that is ready to record. This order keeps things moving.

  • Pull the city's electronic property file for your address to see permits and code cases.
  • Complete the Wisconsin Real Estate Condition Report so it is ready the moment a contract is accepted.
  • Get a payoff figure from your lender and a copy of your current tax bill.
  • Decide whether to list with an agent, sell it yourself, or ask cash buyers for written offers that show fees and the closing date.
  • Confirm who will prepare the deed and file the electronic transfer return.

A cash buyer can shorten the middle of that list, since there is usually no mortgage appraisal, but each step still happens in some form.

Oshkosh is the Winnebago County seat with about 67,460 residents. Owners occupy 55.0 percent of the 27,451 households. The median owner-occupied value is $177,700. Owners typically pay $1,362 a month with a mortgage and $635 without, median gross rent is $935, and median household income is $62,188. Treat these as background. Recent sales near your address say more about price than a citywide median.

The University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh has a campus downtown, so some buyers will want to rent to students. Two rules matter for them. A city ordinance bars more than four unrelated people in one living unit unless the dwelling operates as a rooming house. And parking on lawns or unmarked areas in the university area draws citations of $232 per day. If your house has been a rental, gather any inspection records for the buyer. Rental complaint and inspection details sit on the city's rental inspections page.

An Oshkosh tax bill carries four rates: the City of Oshkosh, Winnebago County, the Oshkosh Area School District and Fox Valley Technical College. The assessor does not issue bills or set the rate. A levy increase or a referendum can raise your tax even when your assessed value stays flat. Special assessments and unpaid utility bills can add to a bill, so clear them before a buyer's title company finds them.

To dispute a value, go to Open Book first and the Board of Review second. Contact the City Clerk at least 48 hours before the Board of Review to get an objection form. By the time a December tax bill arrives, it is too late to file. The Board has five regular members and two alternates serving five-year terms, and it weighs only the evidence presented at the hearing, such as recent comparable sales. Call (920) 236-5070 to ask the assessor about the next cycle.

Oshkosh Inspection Services issues building permits and takes applications online. You may need a permit for new construction, additions, remodels, garages and sheds, decks and porches, siding and roofing, doors and windows other than sash replacement, electrical, plumbing and heating and cooling work, pools, fences, patios, driveways and demolition. Interior painting, flooring and replacing a faucet need none. Nothing may begin until the permit is issued and paid for.

Two details catch sellers off guard. Demolition, including a garage, requires a plumbing permit to disconnect water and sewer first, and no more than one layer of old shingles may remain under new ones. The city also keeps electronic property files showing permits, cases and projects. Records before 1997 are still being scanned, so call 920-236-5048 to ask whether your address is complete. Ask what fee schedule applies when you pull a permit.

An owner selling a home of one to four units owes the buyer a completed Real Estate Condition Report within 10 days after the contract is accepted (Wis. Stat. 709.02). If the report is late, the buyer may rescind within two business days after the 10 days end and recover deposits. Wis. Stat. 709.01 excuses court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the property and transfers exempt from the transfer fee.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Winnebago County
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Winnebago County Register of Deeds. It must carry the grantor's notarized signature, a legal description, a return address and the parcel number from the tax bill. Only the original deed with original signatures can be recorded, and the electronic transfer return receipt must come with it. Call 920-232-3394 with questions.

Winnebago County Register of Deeds charges
ServiceCharge
Recording a deed or other standard document$30 flat
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page
Certified copyAdd $1 for the certificate
State transfer fee$3 per $1,000 of value, rounded up to the next hundred

The transfer fee comes from Wis. Stat. 77.22 and falls on the seller. The office accepts cash, money order or personal check, and cards only for in-office orders with a $2.50 surcharge on amounts up to $50.

The Oshkosh Area School District runs two high schools, Oshkosh North and Oshkosh West, and Fox Valley Technical College has a campus in the city. Buyers with children will ask about attendance areas, so find out which school covers your address and say so in the listing.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Oshkosh rental house with students living in it?
faqs.a: Yes, but read the lease first and give the buyer the facts. The housing code caps an ordinary living unit at four unrelated occupants unless it operates as a rooming house, and parking citations in the university area are $232 per day. Share any inspection history.

faqs.q: Who sets my Oshkosh property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City of Oshkosh, Winnebago County, the Oshkosh Area School District and Fox Valley Technical College. The city assessor does not set the rate or issue bills.

faqs.q: When can I contest my Oshkosh assessment?
faqs.a: Through Open Book and then the Board of Review. Ask the City Clerk for an objection form at least 48 hours before the Board meets, since a December tax bill arrives too late for an objection. The assessor's number is (920) 236-5070.

faqs.q: Can I record a photocopy of my Oshkosh deed?
faqs.a: No. Winnebago County records only the original deed with original signatures. The grantor's signature must be notarized, and the electronic transfer return receipt must be filed first and brought with the deed and the $30 fee.

faqs.q: How do I find permits on my Oshkosh house?
faqs.a: Ask Inspection Services at 920-236-5048. The city keeps electronic property files for permits, cases and projects. Documents before 1997 are still being scanned, so staff can tell you whether your address is complete.
